title: Compatibility Matrix and Deprecation Playbook for Component Library
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Goal: Create a practical, implementation-focused playbook that governs how we evaluate, communicate, and execute deprecations across the design system (tokens, buttons, tables, charts). The playbook will include: a compatibility matrix format, semantic compatibility rules (visual, API, behavioral), deprecation timelines and communication templates, migration guides and codemod strategy, QA/visual diff requirements, and Console/Docs UX for showing deprecation notices. This ticket ties together design stewardship with engineering rollout requirements and PM communication plans.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix published in Confluence and linked from DS docs
Deprecation RFC reviewed and approved by Design Lead and Eng owners
Migration guide for tokens and primary button variants written and validated in a sample app
At least one codemod prototype for button prop renames (JSX/TSX) available in repo
Console deprecation banner design and copy finalized and queued for implementation
Checklist for visual regression tests added to DS CI pipeline
checklist: Define matrix columns: component, affected props, visual impact, API change, semantic change, recommended action, migration cost
Agree on semantic versioning rules for components (major/minor/patch) and document mapping to deprecation severity
Draft deprecation communication templates for: release notes, in-console banners, GitHub PR/Issue templates, and email to enterprise customers
Design migration flows and small-viewport UX for replacing deprecated tokens in style editor
Partner with Eng to estimate effort for codemods and automated tests
Schedule cross-team review session (Design, Eng, PM, Docs)

notes: Trade-offs: aggressive auto-migration (codemods) reduces customer effort but increases risk for edge-case runtime behavior in apps with custom wrappers.
Decision: Use a two-track deprecation cadence — low-risk cosmetic token changes use 8-week window; API/behavior changes use 16-week window plus canary deployment requirement.
Observation: Charts library has more fragile consumers due to data-shape contracts; recommend stricter API deprecation policy for charts (longer window + example-driven migration guides).
Constraints: On-prem customers may be on older runtime; deprecation banners in Console must include an opt-out timeline and explicit upgrade steps for Private deployments.
decisions: Adopt matrix-based classification (Cosmetic / Non-breaking API / Breaking API) with mapped timelines
Require a migration guide and at least one sample app demonstrating upgrade path before marking deprecation as 'Ready'
All deprecations with high customer impact must have PM-approved communication and a dedicated rollback plan
